s1.syndrome_frame: A chronic cutaneous lesion with crusts and irregular shape, presenting with dermal infiltration and variable response to immunotherapy
salient_findings: Irregularly shaped 5 × 3 cm plaque with multiple superficial crusts
Infiltration of the reticular dermis by eosinophilic keratinocytes with pleomorphic nuclei
Variable response to cemiplimab with marked regression of the primary plaque but emergence of new papular lesions
key_facts: 59-year-old man with a crusty lesion in the right fronto-orbital region
Lesion present for several months
No significant past medical history
Excisional biopsy showed lobules and detached aggregates of eosinophilic keratinocytes
Pleomorphic nuclei and prominent nucleoli were observed
No clear evidence of basaloid nests
Treatment with cemiplimab 350 mg every 3 weeks was initiated
18F-FDG PET/CT demonstrated a focal area of uptake in the supraorbital lesion
Marked regression of the plaque after five cycles of therapy
Emergence of new papular lesions with features typical of basal cell carcinoma

shortlist.label: Basal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: New papular lesions with features typical of basal cell carcinoma emerged during treatment

shortlist.label: Keratoacanthoma
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of a crusty lesion with irregular shape and dermal infiltration

shortlist.label: Bowen's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Variable response to immunotherapy and presence of pleomorphic nuclei

shortlist.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive nature of the lesion and presence of pleomorphic nuclei and prominent nucleoli

raw.rationale: The excisional biopsy showed lobules and detached aggregates of eosinophilic keratinocytes with pleomorphic nuclei and prominent nucleoli, which is consistent with invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma. The initial response to cemiplimab, a treatment for squamous cell carcinoma, further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Although new papular lesions with features typical of basal cell carcinoma emerged during treatment, the initial biopsy and response to cemiplimab suggest that the primary lesion was invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.

rejected.label: Keratoacanthoma
rejected.why: Keratoacanthoma typically presents as a solitary, rapidly growing nodule with a central crater, which does not match the description of the lesion in the vignette.

rejected.label: Bowen's disease
rejected.why: Bowen's disease is a form of squamous cell carcinoma in situ, but the biopsy showed invasion into the reticular dermis, indicating invasive disease.

rejected.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Merkel cell carcinoma is a rare, aggressive tumor with a distinct histological appearance, which was not described in the biopsy results.
